![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/43cff74165732892223841f6780e7aa22c024e3b3c173e60ce15d8d6841a5a08.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $y={x}^{2}-1$ and $y=-\frac{3}{2}x$ for $x\in [-2,\frac{1}{2}]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=5.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
Let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/7aad98fe0513514aa8827bea4e9ffbac5b70bcb8da7923effd789988c81e286f.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y=-\frac{3}{2}x,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y={x}^{2}-1.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y={x}^{2}-1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/623b59b7aca8b33c6149ac6b0916d1eeb425adc3f74568868383806cd9b03b12.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}[\,(5)-({x}^{2}-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}{[6-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=-\frac{3}{2}x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/c0467a3bf02287589f897586a1358e4abb02759134b6b58622125319dc7331da.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}{[\,(5)-(-\frac{3}{2}x)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}{[5+\frac{3}{2}x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}{[6-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}{[5+\frac{3}{2}x]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{1/2}({[6-{x}^{2}]}^{2}-{[5+\frac{3}{2}x]}^{2})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
